purpose: Capture a DOST-published account of Isabela State University's Freshwater Fisheries R&D Center and retain its named possible ludong fishing-ground locations as unresolved research leads.

source.title: Science for Change
source.publisher: Department of Science and Technology (DOST), Philippines
source.rightsReview: No item-specific reuse license was identified in the reviewed pages. No photographs or extended text were copied; cite the DOST publication and do not infer image or dataset reuse permission.

programContext.institution: Isabela State University Freshwater Fisheries R&D Center
programContext.projectScope: Conservation, artificial spawning and culture techniques, and gathering information on natural habitats; a separate project covers freshwater eel culture and aquatic-plant feed research.
programContext.siteDiscoveryClaim: The DOST account says the project identified 11 municipalities that could be fishing grounds for ludong.
programContext.evidenceType: Program summary and reported possible fishing-ground leads, not a fish collection checklist, voucher dataset, survey methods report, occurrence export, or legal fishing-rule source.

verbatimMunicipalityLeads.sourceLocationText: Abuan River in Cabisera 10 and Ilagis River

verbatimMunicipalityLeads.localityReview: The source pairs Maconacon with Reina Mercedes; preserve this wording as an unresolved locality crosswalk.

verbatimMunicipalityLeads.sourceLocationText: Dialaoayo, Pinacanauan River in Didiuan and Ilaya
verbatimMunicipalityLeads.localityReview: The punctuation does not make clear whether these are one or several place/site relationships; do not assign a river reach from this line alone.

dataQualityLimits: The source labels the 11 municipalities as places that could be fishing grounds; it does not publish dates, sampling methods, effort, exact stations, vouchers, photographs linked to specimens, or taxon-by-site records.
The account uses Cestraeus sp. for its project scope. It does not establish which species or species-level taxon was present at each named lead.
The phrase 'Blues River in Reina Mercedes' is preserved verbatim and is not silently attached to Maconacon or another municipality.
The Palanan line combines Dialaoayo, Pinacanauan River, Didiuan, and Ilaya without an unambiguous relationship; keep each as a research label only.
A separate passage refers to Blue River in Isabela; no identity link to the panel's 'Blues River' was established.
A program leader's statement that ludong can only be fished in Cagayan River is not a current legal rule or a site-specific occurrence dataset.
No named-site geometry, current presence, catchability, natural diet, fishing access, water safety, or legal status was established.
nextAction: Screen the source's location labels against the local Region II GeoNames candidate queue, keeping name matches and source locality conflicts separate; seek the underlying Freshwater Fisheries R&D Center survey, station list, specimen records, and reuse conditions.
